sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: age rules for the safety course, fee eras, record types, habitual violator tiers, SR22 stays and court-related suspensions
Confusable pairs among the points, insurance and suspension rules, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
Drivers 21 or older can be required to take the safety course after two or more convictions within 12 months, while drivers under 21 can be required after two or more convictions with no time window stated. [A01]
Why it matters: group safety course; confusable adult versus under-twenty-one trigger.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A03
Older no-insurance suspensions dated before Jan. 1, 2015 carry lower reinstatement fees of $150, $225 and $300 for the first, second and third or later suspension. [A03]
Why it matters: group reinstatement fees; confusable pre-2015 versus post-2015 tiers.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A04
Failing a chemical test means a 180-day suspension, whereas refusing it means a full year, or two years when the driver has a prior intoxicated-driving conviction. [A04]
Why it matters: group chemical tests; confusable fail versus refuse.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A05
The free Viewable Driver Record cannot be printed and is not official, while the Official Driver Record costs $4 and can be printed for up to 30 days after purchase. [A05]
Why it matters: group driver records; confusable viewable versus official.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A05
Two injury-or-death judgments within 10 years bring a 10-year habitual violator suspension, but when both are for intoxicated or .08 driving causing death the suspension is for life. [A05]
Why it matters: group habitual violators; confusable ten-year versus life.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A05
Under Section B, three judgments within 10 years from the listed major offenses, including intoxicated driving or a BAC of .08 or more, bring a 10-year suspension. [A05]
Why it matters: group habitual violators; confusable two-judgment versus three-judgment tiers.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A06
Offenses counted under Section B also include reckless driving, drag racing or a speed contest, leaving the scene of an accident, resisting law enforcement and any felony involving a motor vehicle. [A06]
Why it matters: group habitual violators; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A06
The manual's example of a Section C habitual violator is a person with nine speeding tickets and one reckless driving conviction within 10 years, who faces a 5-year suspension. [A06]
Why it matters: group habitual violators; worked example.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A06
Operating a vehicle without ever having obtained a driver's license is one of the offenses that can complete the Section C count of 10 violations. [A06]
Why it matters: group habitual violators; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A06
Anyone with court-granted specialized driving privileges must keep an SR22 on file for the whole period, keep the court order with them or in the vehicle, show it to police on request and carry a valid credential. [A06]
Why it matters: group specialized privileges; link to SR22.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A06
Restriction 2 is no longer added to records for habitual violator suspensions or habitual violator probationary licenses expiring on or after January 1, 2015. [A06]
Why it matters: group restrictions; confusable Restriction 2 versus Restriction 5.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A03
An SR26 received during the 180-day stay of an indefinite no-insurance suspension removes the stay and makes the suspension active again, and any stayed fees become due again. [A03]
Why it matters: group SR22; confusable stay versus termination.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A03
A suspension for missing court or not paying a ticket can be stayed by keeping an SR22 on file for as long as the suspension lasts. [A03]
Why it matters: group court suspensions; link to SR22.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A03
Reinstatement fees can be paid on myBMV.com, by phone, at a BMV Connect kiosk, or by mail with the coupon the BMV sends. [A03]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; dynamic service detail.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A02
When the vehicle was company-owned or rented, the employer or rental company completes the affidavit on State Form 55434 to prove financial responsibility. [A02]
Why it matters: group insurance proof; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A02
A driver suspended earlier for not proving insurance can be asked to verify insurance again after any later pointable moving violation. [A02]
Why it matters: group insurance proof; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A02
Anyone convicted by an Indiana or out-of-state court of driving uninsured must contact that court to learn whether showing proof of insurance can remove the conviction. [A02]
Why it matters: group insurance proof; scope note court versus BMV.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A01
A BMV-approved Driver Safety Program is a defensive driving course offered in classroom, online or DVD formats. [A01]
Why it matters: group safety course; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A04
When a driver under 18 is cited for intoxicated driving, the Juvenile Court may also recommend a suspension. [A04]
Why it matters: group impaired driving; teen link.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A04
Reckless watercraft operation that endangers others, or running a boat while your driving privileges are suspended, is also added to the driver record. [A04]
Why it matters: group watercraft; link to boating rules.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A04
A court that finds a parent behind on child support may have the BMV suspend that parent's driving privileges at once until the court orders reinstatement. [A04]
Why it matters: group other suspensions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A04
A local child support enforcement agency can also order a suspension that lasts until the parent pays or sets up a payment plan. [A04]
Why it matters: group other suspensions; confusable court order versus agency order.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A05
After a court's requirements are met, the court sends reinstatement information to the BMV, which may need up to 10 business days to process it. [A05]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A05
The Reinstatement Requirements box near the top of a driver record lists any outstanding requirements and the date the driver becomes eligible for reinstatement. [A05]
Why it matters: group driver records; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]
